$comment: One statement of the rule for judging a pointer and length against a
WebAssembly linear memory, checked in both hosts.
host/src/kernel-scratch.ts, which keep their own arithmetic because a
bounds check runs on the syscall hot path and a wasm module call per
check is a cost the performance contract does not permit.
So the two hosts share a STATEMENT rather than an implementation, and the
statement is failable. Every limit is a whole number of 64 KiB pages so
the TypeScript half can build a real WebAssembly.Memory of that size
`rustOnly` marks a case the TypeScript half cannot express, with the
reason. Saying which properties a technique cannot reach is part of the
result; a silently-skipped case reads exactly like a passing one.

cases.name: a zero-length range at address zero is legal
a null pointer with a positive length is refused
cases.why: Address zero is addressable in wasm; a kernel allocator returning zero means failure, and that convention is what is being enforced.

cases.name: a failed allocation is a null pointer, not an out-of-bounds range
cases.why: addr 0 with len 1000000 is BOTH null and past a 1-page memory. The rule names the null pointer, because 0 is what a kernel allocator returns when it gave nothing: reporting the memory's extent would diagnose the wrong fact. No other case in this file has a null address that is also out of bounds, so this is the only one that fixes the order of the two checks.

cases.name: allowing address zero does not waive the bounds check
cases.why: allowAddressZero says the caller means offset zero; it does not say the range fits. Without this case a rule that returns ok for any zero address once the flag is set passes the whole file.

cases.name: a caller that means offset zero says so
the exact end of memory is inclusive
one byte past the end is refused
a zero-length range AT the end is legal
cases.why: end == limit, which the rule admits; it addresses no byte.

cases.name: a zero-length range past the end is refused
cases.why: Nothing is read, but the address is not one this memory has.

cases.name: a range that spans a grown memory is admitted
the largest wasm32 address with a positive length is refused
cases.why: A 32-bit pointer at its maximum plus any length leaves every real memory.

cases.name: an address that overflows the address space is refused as overflow
cases.why: Unreachable through a wasm32 pointer, and the TypeScript half cannot present it for a memory64 guest either -- but not because of a 32-bit ceiling, which does not apply there. `checkedWasmGuestPointerOffset` accepts the u64, then refuses any address above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER with "pointer exceeds JavaScript's exact address range", before a range is considered. The boundary is that a JavaScript host cannot name an address it cannot represent exactly. Kept because crates/host-native takes a u64 from a memory64 guest and has no such limit.
